items.evidence: The reload step (lines 93-95) reads the name field and the page-header title back from the server, so both would still show "E2E Hoodie" if the save never ran.
AC1 is asserted after save at line 87 (header title, plus the document title at 88). AC2 is asserted after reload at lines 94-95 (name field and header title).
The suite has no product page object or products-grid helper; the existing pages cover only orders, drafts, the address dialog, home and login. Nothing in pages/lib/scenarios is duplicated.
There is no waitForTimeout or sleep. The toPass block retries on a named condition (the anchor href), not on a fixed delay.
The spec imports test from fixtures/test.ts, uses ORDERS_SCENARIO, is not tagged parallel() and writes nothing to the cache or dumps.

e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts:47 finds the product row through Glide's generated cell ids (`td[role="gridcell"][id^="glide-cell-1-"]`) and a column index, then clicks by computed pixel coordinates. That is a generated-id, positional selector rather than a test-id or role locator.
The product comes from the orders scenario (PRODUCTS.hoodie). The spec only navigates to it and creates no data.
No database ids are hard-coded; the product is found by the scenario's known name, PRODUCTS.hoodie.name.
The spec uses the default admin stored session, has no UI sign-in and contains no credentials.
The spec is in e2e/tests/products/ and check-types:e2e exits 0.

e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts:31 defines all locators (search input, grid, name input, save button, header, toast) and the multi-step open-from-grid action inline in the spec instead of on a ProductPage page object.
The change adds no page object, so the page-object style rule does not apply.
The test has `// Arrange` and `// Act & Assert` comments (lines 28, 39).
It is one test with three test.step stages: open, rename and save, reload and verify.
The title describes the behaviour and carries #e2e.
The header block comment at lines 13-16 says what the spec covers and why.
Assertions are web-first. The attribute and bounding-box reads feed hover geometry; no page text is asserted on as a copied value.
e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts:44 types the scenario product name into the URL regex (`/query=E2E(%20|\+)Hoodie/`) instead of deriving it from PRODUCTS.hoodie.name.
There is no cleanup code and no unique or timestamped names.
e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts:56 puts explicit `{ timeout: 1000 }` on getAttribute, boundingBox and toHaveAttribute (lines 56, 58, 67) without saying why.
Relative imports keep the .ts extension, and test and expect come only from the fixture.
The spec has no any, no casts and no gql calls.

e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts:41 has numbered comments that narrate the next line ("// 2. Navigate to /products/...", "// 4. Fill the Name textbox", "// 5. Click Save", "// 6. Reload the product page") and are copied from the plan.

structured_output.summary: The test covers both acceptance criteria and proves the rename was saved by reading the name field and page title back after a reload. It also uses the suite's fixture and the orders scenario correctly. One blocker: it finds the product row through Glide's generated cell ids and clicks by computed pixel coordinates (B6). Minor issues: all locators and the multi-step grid action are inline in the spec instead of on a page object; the product name is typed into a URL regex instead of using PRODUCTS.hoodie.name; there are unexplained 1000 ms timeouts; and numbered comments narrate the steps.
